decree_letter.body:
The Remounts — Dejean, Minister of War Administration
An affair of state, Sire: a bill of your own acts, laid before you by the office it touches. Each answer is priced on its button; Not Now sets it aside; left unanswered by the date, it takes the second answer for you.
Sire, the depots hold more saddles than horses. A credit now buys remounts in the country at the spring fairs' price, not the campaign's.
Historically the cavalry was remounted between campaigns by purchase and requisition — the Prussian studs after Jena, the depots that refilled the squadrons before Friedland.
❧ The cavalry depots hold 17,700 of 30,000 (59%); the weakest squadrons stand at 100% of their establishment; the chest holds 5,000 gold against 1,500.
WHAT EACH ANSWER DOES
  Buy the remounts: 1 administrative action (1 left today); 1,500 gold (the treasury holds 5,000); cavalry levies cost 20% less (×0.8) until Late April 1806, 8 turns.
  Let the depots wait: no change.
  Decree it: 1 administrative action (1 left today); Authority 90 → 87 — the marshals' calm holds above 70; cavalry levies cost 20% less (×0.8) until Late April 1806, 8 turns.
If unanswered by Early January 1806: Let the depots wait — no change.
